sentences.cn_text: 哈佛大学一项新调查发现，超过三分之二的美国年轻人不认同特朗普总统使用推特的做法。
sentences.en_text: A new survey by Harvard University finds more than two-thirds of young Americans disapprove of President Trump’s use of Twitter.

sentences.cn_text: 这表明千禧一代更倾向于通过其他渠道获取白宫新闻，而非总统的社交媒体平台。
sentences.en_text: The implication is that Millennials prefer news from the White House to be filtered through other sources, not a president’s social media platform.

sentences.cn_text: 大多数美国人依赖社交媒体查看每日头条新闻。
sentences.en_text: Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines.

sentences.cn_text: 然而，随着对所有媒体的不信任感上升,人们可能开始提升其媒体素养技能。
sentences.en_text: Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills.

sentences.cn_text: 这种趋势十分必要。
sentences.en_text: Such a trend is badly needed.

sentences.cn_text: 牛津大学研究显示，在2016年总统竞选期间，政治关键州密歇根州的推特用户分享的网络内容中，近四分之一为虚假新闻。
sentences.en_text: During the 2016 presidential campaign, nearly a quarter of web content shared by Twitter users in the politically critical state of Michigan was fake news, according to the University of Oxford.

sentences.cn_text: 为BuzzFeed新闻开展的一项调查发现，44%的脸书用户很少或从不信任来自这家媒体巨头的新闻。
sentences.en_text: And a survey conducted for BuzzFeed News found 44 percent of Facebook users rarely or never trust news from the media giant.

sentences.cn_text: 作为数字原住民的年轻人确实在网络空间中更加善于区分事实与虚构。
sentences.en_text: Young people who are digital natives are indeed becoming more skillful at separating fact from fiction in cyberspace.

sentences.cn_text: 骑士基金会对14至24岁年轻人的焦点小组调查发现，他们使用「分布式信任」来验证信息的真实性。
sentences.en_text: A Knight Foundation focus-group survey of young people between ages 14 and 24 found they use “distributed trust” to verify stories.

sentences.cn_text: 他们交叉核对信息来源，更青睐来自不同视角的新闻——尤其是那些对任何偏见开诚布公的新闻。
sentences.en_text: They cross-check sources and prefer news from different perspectives — especially those that are open about any bias.

sentences.cn_text: 调查总结道：「许多年轻人认为自己对自我教育负有很大的个人责任，并积极寻求对立观点。」
sentences.en_text: “Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing viewpoints,” the survey concluded.

sentences.cn_text: 这种主动探究可能会产生另一种影响。
sentences.en_text: Such active research can have another effect.

sentences.cn_text: 威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校2014年在澳大利亚、英国和美国开展的一项调查发现，年轻人对社交媒体的依赖促进了更高的政治参与度。
sentences.en_text: A 2014 survey conducted in Australia, Britain, and the United States by the University of Wisconsin-Madison found that young people’s reliance on social media led to greater political engagement.

sentences.cn_text: 社交媒体使用户能够更亲近、更即时地体验新闻事件，同时也允许他们转发新闻以展示自己的价值观和兴趣。
sentences.en_text: Social media allows users to experience news events more intimately and immediately while also permitting them to re-share news as a projection of their values and interests.

sentences.cn_text: 这促使用户更加意识到自己在传播信息中的角色。
sentences.en_text: This forces users to be more conscious of their role in passing along information.

sentences.cn_text: 巴纳研究集团的一项调查发现，美国人认为假新闻现象的首要原因是「读者错误」，而非虚构报道或报道中的事实错误。
sentences.en_text: A survey by Barna research group found the top reason given by Americans for the fake news phenomenon is “reader error,” more so than made-up stories or factual mistakes in reporting.

sentences.cn_text: 约三分之一的人认为假新闻问题在于通过社交媒体对真实新闻的「曲解或夸大」。
sentences.en_text: About a third say the problem of fake news lies in “misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news” via social media.

sentences.cn_text: 换言之，在社交媒体上分享新闻的选择可能是问题的核心。
sentences.en_text: In other words, the choice to share news on social media may be the heart of the issue.

sentences.cn_text: 巴纳集团主编罗克珊·斯通表示：「这表明在应对这一问题上确实存在真实的个人责任。」
sentences.en_text: “This indicates there is a real personal responsibility in counteracting this problem,” says Roxanne Stone, editor in chief at Barna Group.

sentences.cn_text: 因此，当年轻人批评一位过度发推的总统时，他们展现出思维能力上的心智自律——以及他们在社交媒体分享时机选择上的自律。
sentences.en_text: So when young people are critical of an over-tweeting president, they reveal a mental discipline in thinking skills — and in their choices on when to share on social media.
